summary: Synthistat Ltd's non-confidential business development summary describes a multi-target HDAC inhibitor platform comprising 14 small-molecule candidates with computationally predicted (docking) activity against HDAC2/6, BRD4, PARP1, and dopamine D2R. All evidence presented is computational (molecular docking, predicted physicochemical/ADME properties); no wet-lab experimental data are reported. The platform is at an early discovery/computational stage, seeking partners for in-vitro biology and translational development, with provisional patent protection in place.

content_blocks.title: Executive Summary – Multi-Target HDAC Inhibitor Platform
content_blocks.content: Synthistat Ltd is developing multi-target epigenetic therapeutics that combine HDAC inhibition, BRD4 modulation, PARP1 inhibition, and (in advanced embodiments) dopamine D2R regulation within a single small-molecule scaffold. The platform uses a modular pharmacophore: Novel cap – Programmed linker – Zinc-binding group. The novel cap moiety acts as a global conformational director, preventing intramolecular folding, enforcing extended binding geometries, improving engagement of HDAC/BRD4/PARP1, and enhancing metabolic stability. No wet-lab experimental data are presented; all activity claims are computational predictions.

content_blocks.title: Core Molecular Innovation – Linker Design
content_blocks.content: The linker is intentionally engineered (often conformationally constrained) to encode exit-vector control, three-dimensional geometry, and expansion of target scope into GPCR space (D2R). This design is claimed to allow multi-target engagement without sacrificing epigenetic pharmacology. All described properties are design rationale, not empirical results.

content_blocks.title: Integrated Multi-Target Activity Summary (Predicted)
content_blocks.content:
Summary of predicted functional outcomes per target class:
- HDAC2/HDAC6: Robust zinc-coordinated predicted inhibition with pose-verified non-covalent geometry.
- BRD4: Strong predicted engagement across the 14 dual-target candidates, with recurrent Asn140-directed recognition geometries.
- PARP1: Additional predicted engagement in 9 of the 14 current HDAC/BRD4 candidates.
- D2R (HDAC-008): High-affinity predicted D2R engagement (-10.1 kcal/mol) in the advanced dual-target lead.
All values are computational docking scores, not biochemical assay results.

content_blocks.title: Docking & ADME Highlights and Prediction Methodology
content_blocks.content:
Key highlights from computational analysis:
- 14 pose-verified candidates show predicted engagement of both HDAC and BRD4.
- All 14 have zero Lipinski violations.
- Predicted logP: ~0.36-2.02; logS: ~-3.67 to -1.74.
- HDAC-031: strongest predicted HDAC2 binding (-9.8 kcal/mol).
- HDAC-006: strongest predicted HDAC6 binding (-8.6 kcal/mol).
- HDAC-032 and HDAC-035: strongest predicted BRD4 binding (-9.1 kcal/mol).
- 9 of 14 candidates have PARP1 docking scores; HDAC-008 has D2R score of -10.1 kcal/mol.

Prediction Methodology: logP and logS generated using trained molecular graph-based regression models with 2D cheminformatics descriptors. These are model-specific predictions, not fragment-based or linear descriptor calculations.

Lead Evolution Strategy (HDAC-007 → HDAC-008): preserve HDAC/BRD4/PARP1 pharmacology, reprogram linker geometry, unlock D2R engagement without destabilising core HDAC/BRD4 binding. Described as 'encoded polypharmacology, not empirical promiscuity.'

content_blocks.title: Primary Oncology Applications and Strategic Differentiation
content_blocks.content:
Target indications:
- Acute Myeloid Leukaemia (AML)
- MYC-driven & super-enhancer-dependent cancers
- HR-deficient tumours (breast, ovarian, prostate, pancreatic, lung, glioblastoma)

Additional commercial application: Enhancement of lentiviral vector production (LVV) for CAR-T, gene therapy, and CRISPR manufacturing.

Strategic Differentiation vs. Conventional HDACi:
- Multi-target integration: Yes (Novel) vs. No (Conventional)
- HDAC+BRD4: Yes (14 candidates) vs. No
- HDAC+BRD4+PARP1: Yes (9 candidates) vs. No
- D2R modulation: Yes (HDAC-008) vs. No
- Conformational control: Engineered vs. Absent
- Michael acceptors: None vs. Common
- Developability: High vs. Limited
All differentiation claims are based on computational predictions, not experimental data.

content_blocks.title: Ligand Pose Verification & Structural Robustness
content_blocks.content:
Multi-target activity supported by ligand-pose verification across independent docking campaigns using multiple receptor structures, cavity definitions, and docking engines. 14 candidates have pose-verified predicted activity at both HDAC and BRD4. 9 extend into predicted HDAC-BRD4-PARP1 tri-target profile; HDAC-008 additionally carries D2R score.

Structural metrics across dual set:
- HDAC zinc-donor distance: ~1.77-2.20 Å
- BRD4 Asn140 ND2-to-acceptor distances: ~2.8-3.2 Å
- Three-anchor architecture: (A) cap-mediated surface recognition/conformational control, (B) linker-mediated directional steering, (C) zinc-binding-group coordination in HDAC.

Development & Partnering status:
- Provisional patent protection in place
- Multiple validated lead series (computationally)
- Extensive structural & docking verification
- Ready for in-vitro biology & translational development (not yet initiated)
- Seeking partnership; additional confidential data available under NDA.

content_blocks.title: Older Series – HDAC/D2R Dual-Mechanism Candidate Therapeutics (Separate Provisional Filing)
content_blocks.content:
An earlier/separate series of small-molecule candidates designed via structure-guided computational methods to engage HDAC2/6 and D2R simultaneously. Scientific rationale: HDAC inhibition is established in AML (San José-Enériz et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2021); D2R antagonism (thioridazine) selectively eliminates leukemic progenitor populations in AML (Sachlos et al., 2012), validating D2R as a target in AML pathobiology.

Computational results for older series (Molecules 1-4):
- HDAC2 binding: down to -8.5 kcal/mol
- D2R engagement: down to -10.7 kcal/mol (potential nM potency)
- Favourable solubility, polarity, permeability indicators
- Improved molecular flexibility profiles
- Absence of critical toxicity-associated motifs
All results are computational; no wet-lab data reported.

content_blocks.title: IP Status, Partnering, and References
content_blocks.content:
IP: Structures protected under a provisional patent filing with full priority coverage; not disclosed to external parties. Additional confidential molecular information available under NDA.

key_findings: All activity data are purely computational (molecular docking scores and ML-predicted physicochemical/ADME properties); no wet-lab experimental results (biochemical assays, cell-based assays, in vivo studies) are reported anywhere in the document.
14 pose-verified small-molecule candidates show predicted dual engagement of HDAC (HDAC2/HDAC6) and BRD4, all with zero Lipinski violations and no PAINS alerts.
9 of 14 candidates additionally show predicted PARP1 engagement (docking scores -9.6 to -11.4 kcal/mol), and HDAC-008 shows predicted D2R engagement (-10.1 kcal/mol).

Strongest predicted HDAC2 binder: HDAC-031 (-9.8 kcal/mol); strongest predicted BRD4 binders: HDAC-032 and HDAC-035 (-9.1 kcal/mol); strongest predicted HDAC6 binder: HDAC-006 (-8.6 kcal/mol); strongest predicted PARP1 binder: HDAC-006 (-11.4 kcal/mol).

Older series (separate provisional filing): 4 molecules with predicted HDAC2 binding down to -8.5 kcal/mol and D2R engagement down to -10.7 kcal/mol; Molecule 3 identified as most promising based on combined ADME and docking profile.
All candidates lack Michael acceptors (a key safety/selectivity advantage over panobinostat, which has a Michael acceptor present).
Provisional patent protection is in place for both the newer multi-target series and the older HDAC/D2R series (separate filings); SMILES and full structures withheld.
Platform is explicitly described as 'ready for in-vitro biology & translational development,' indicating no in-vitro biology has been conducted yet — consistent with TRL 1-2.
Scientific rationale for D2R targeting in AML is supported by published preclinical evidence (Sachlos et al., 2012: thioridazine selectively eliminates D2R-expressing AML progenitors).
Predicted physicochemical properties generated using trained molecular graph-based ML regression models combined with 2D cheminformatics descriptors — not experimental measurements.
Panobinostat used as reference comparator throughout; Synthistat candidates show improved predicted BRD4 engagement and ADME profiles vs. panobinostat across most metrics.
Additional commercial application proposed: enhancement of lentiviral vector production (LVV) for CAR-T, gene therapy, and CRISPR manufacturing — no supporting data provided.
